items.anchor: Ordinary full BFGS often succeeds on nonsmooth objectives
items.reason: motivation: empirical observation reported in the literature (Lewis--Overton [LO]); not a mathematical claim of the article and not used in any proof

items.anchor: We give complementary positive and negative results
items.note: Scope of both families: finite convex objectives, Armijo--weak-Wolfe accepted steps, actual gradients at differentiable accepted iterates (Definition art:admissible for the positive theorems; the failing runs of the negative theorems come from the unit-first search with every query differentiable).

items.anchor: A centered smooth--sublinear theorem proves global whole-sequence convergence
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M7): the abstract now states that the compact initial sublevels lie in the region of the centered representation, as Theorem art:centered assumes. The first half (global whole-sequence convergence for u^2+|v|) is Corollary art:mixed-benchmark. centered_representation_needs_containment shows that the containment cannot be dropped.

items.anchor: Coercive degree-one homogeneous objectives, including coercive max-linear functions, norms and gauges, admit global convergence.
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M41): the families are named, "coercive max-linear functions, norms and gauges" (before: "the stated max-linear and gauge families"). True as phrased: finiteness and convexity, the hypotheses of Theorem art:homogeneous not repeated here, are the standing scope of the abstract ("for finite convex objectives", lines 40-41); "coercive max-linear functions, norms and gauges" are the three families of Corollary art:homogeneous-examples.

items.anchor: Local results cover finite polyhedral smooth-piece partitions
items.note: Summary; true as phrased (coordinator decision, 14 October, overruling the first classification as a discrepancy). It leaves implicit the hypotheses of the summarized results: a unique minimizer and locally C^{1,1} pieces (Theorem art:polyhedral, Corollary art:plq); a unique minimizer, convex C^2 branches, strictly convex low positive sublevels and active-gradient nondegeneracy (Corollary art:planar-max). "Smooth" is informal here; the theorems specify the regularity. The supporting example local_results_need_unique_minimizer (F(u,v)=|v|) only shows that the conclusion x_k -> x_* needs the unique minimizer: its runs converge to another minimizer, so it does not refute the summary.

items.anchor: moving comparison geometry proves convergence although the radial
items.note: Convergence is proved through Corollary art:planar-convergence (moving contour field); the radial criterion is art:radial-condition. The sentence continues "Local results cover ...", so the convergence is local: every infinite admissible run with F(x_0)<1/100.

resolved_discrepancies.description: Theorem art:centered applies to admissible runs whose initial sublevel is compact AND contained in the open convex region U where F = psi + gamma(. - x_*) holds. The abstract says the theorem "applies in arbitrary dimension on compact initial sublevels", omitting the containment. Read for an objective with a local centered representation this is false: the coercive cap of Corollary art:failure_polyhedral equals -1 + max{r_1, -r_1-r_2/8, r_2}, r = x-(-1,16), on the unit sup-norm ball around its minimizer and has compact sublevels, yet its admissible run does not converge to the minimizer (Lean witness). The introduction (introduction.tex:85-88) and Table art:positive-outcomes ("Compact initial sublevel in the structural region") state the containment correctly.
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: A centered smooth--sublinear theorem proves global whole-sequence convergence for $u^2+|v|$ and applies in arbitrary dimension on compact initial sublevels contained in the region of the centered representation.
resolved_discrepancies.resolved: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M7 in TODO_MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW.md); the description quotes the text before the correction, its line numbers are those after it.

resolved_discrepancies.description: Theorem art:local-failure-lower (negative_lower.tex:21-22) says that "The first three branches in this construction are not twice differentiable at zero"; the fourth branch mu||x||^2/2 + x_2 (composed with the fixed whitening x = Az) is a quadratic and is twice differentiable everywhere (Lean witness). "with C^{1,1} branches that lose second differentiability at the accumulation point" reads as a statement about all four branches. The introduction (introduction.tex:77-79) states it correctly ("three of which are not twice differentiable at the minimizer").
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: another retains uniform strong convexity with $C^{1,1}$ branches, three of which lose second differentiability at the accumulation point.
